newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas rises again as volumes remain high.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas rises again as volumes remain high.

text.p: IPE natural gas futures enjoyed another busy day on Tuesday, trading 310 lots after 450 lots had traded on Monday.
Most of the trade, 200 lots, was done in October, where the last deals were done at 10.90 pence a therm, an increase of 0.12 pence from the previous settlement.

A futures broker said there was a lot of interest expected in October when it becomes the spot month as players are keen to trade spot October gas against October 1998 futures. This is because the UK-Continent Interconnector is due to open in October 1998.

There was also trade seen in December, January, February and June. December saw the biggest rise, trading at 14.75 pence a therm, up by 0.325 pence from Monday's settlement. January and February were also up, although June softened, settling 0.22 pence down on the day.

A spokeswoman for the IPE said many players had avoided trading futures in the days before the announcement of details of the Transco storage tender. Now that this has been published, several players are returning to the market, she said.
Front month August was bid at 9.35 pence and offered at 10.00 pence at the close of trade.
